Learn how to build production-ready AI applications and agents powered by Azure SQL. In this hands-on lab, you'll prepare Azure SQL Database as a resilient RAG data source, implement hybrid search that combines vector and keyword retrieval, and integrate your retrieval layer with applications and AI agents. Leave with practical patterns you can apply immediately to build reliable, scalable AI solutions.

embeddingContent:
Continuous improvement for agents: From open source to Foundry

Take a working agent that misses its target and apply continuous improvement: a repeatable process for making one measured change at a time. Use open-source ASSERT to generate evaluations and test data from requirements, create scoring criteria with rubrics, and implement controls with Agent Control Specification (ACS). Then run live with Microsoft Foundry models, the first step toward production, and use GitHub Copilot with the run-assert-eval skill to automate the improvement loop.

Design multi-model routing for AI efficiency with NVIDIA Switchyard

Modern AI applications demand flexibility because different tasks require different models. In this hands-on lab, deploy NVIDIA NeMo Switchyard, an open-source LLM traffic router, on Azure with Microsoft Foundry. Switchyard's stage-based routing directs each request to the right model, escalating to a more capable one only when needed, without changing your application code. Walk away with a multi-model strategy you can apply to your own AI workloads.

This Lab requires you to bring your own laptop. Add this session to your schedule to reserve your seat, as capacity is limited. Please arrive at least 5 minutes early; unclaimed seats may be released to standby attendees.

embeddingContent: Improve token efficiency with vLLM Semantic Router In this lab, you'll build a single endpoint for multiple models on AMD Instinct™ GPUs and use vLLM Semantic Router to match each request to the right model. Route simple tasks to smaller models and complex work to larger ones to save tokens and compute, while keeping sensitive requests on trusted local models. Connect an agent, explore routing decisions, and put your skills to the test by building your own router in a short challenge.

embeddingContent: Proxy, host, operator: Who can read your agent's prompts? Every hop between an agent and a GPU can expose a prompt, and agent loops repeat that exposure with every plan, tool call and retry. For regulated data, strategy or source code, that's a dealbreaker. Richard Rizk, Co-Founder and CTO of BLACKBOX AI, shows how prompts can be sealed on the client and decrypted only inside an attested GPU enclave, taking the proxy, host and operator out of the trust equation.

embeddingContent: All or nothing: Distributed transactions in Azure Cosmos DB What if 'all or nothing' just worked across your whole database? In 15 minutes, go deep on ACID-compliant distributed transactions in Azure Cosmos DB: atomic multi-item writes across partitions and containers, serializable isolation, and automatic rollback when anything fails. We'll live-code the classic move-money-and-place-order scenario, look at how two-phase commit works under the hood, and cover where it fits today. If you've been hand-rolling consistency, this one's for you.

embeddingContent: Can You Trust Your Fabric Data Agent? Test It and Prove It A fluent answer is not the same as a correct one. In a live Fabric demonstration, we expose how broad schema selection, undefined business terms and weak examples make a data agent return plausible but wrong answers. Then we fix it: tighten the schema, improve the instructions, add example queries and rerun a fixed benchmark. The generated T-SQL stays on screen throughout. Leave able to test a Fabric data agent, measure improvement and defend the result to a business sponsor.

embeddingContent:
Confidently Wrong: What Bad Data Does to Good Agents

An agent running on bad data doesn't crash. It answers confidently, it's wrong, and somebody acts on it. Before two agents went live, we had to decide whether the data underneath could be trusted with a business decision: a heavy equipment onboarding agent, and a Microsoft Fabric modernization for a global energy operator. Neither was ready on day one. We'll show the governance work each one needed, what broke early, and a short checklist to run before you hand your next agent the keys.

embeddingContent:
Same Migration, Two Payouts: How Your Routing Decides a Deal's Worth

Two partners move identical workloads to Azure. One earns materially more than the other, and the difference is not technical. It is how the opportunity was routed before any work started. This talk covers that routing decision: when it has to be made, who makes it, who inside Microsoft has to be involved, and what it is worth to get right. Aimed at partners running server, SQL, or VMware migration practices who are leaving money behind without knowing it.

embeddingContent: Two Doors Out of SQL Server: Mirroring vs Change Event Streaming Not everyone's analytics estate lives in one platform. SQL Server 2025 gives you two exits: Mirroring, which lands current-state tables in OneLake, and Change Event Streaming, which pushes row-level change events to Event Hubs, where Fabric Eventstream or Azure Databricks Structured Streaming can pick them up. One is Fabric-native | the other is portable. We'll build the bronze medallion layer on both, and cover why you can only enable one per database.

embeddingContent: Follow one record: What an AI agent will hand over if you ask nicely A shopping assistant built on Azure AI Foundry does its job: answer questions, look up accounts, be helpful. Then someone asks it to confirm a record “for the migration,” and it returns a name, email, Social Security number and full card number. Follow that record from Blob Storage through the agent’s tool call into the answer, trace where data can be exposed on the way, and find the one configuration change separating an agent that leaks from one that refuses, though both look protected.

In this hands-on lab, onboard devices and validate successful onboarding through reporting, configure and target security policies to manage protection settings, and complete device offboarding. Leave with practical experience using Microsoft Intune and Defender to connect IT and Security workflows across onboarding, policy management, and offboarding.

This is a self-paced, digitally-delivered lab experience that you will complete on your own schedule. Click the 'Launch' button to start the lab.

NOTE: This lab will be available to complete on November 17, 2026, starting at 12:00 PM Pacific Time.

Digital Lab: Turning data into agent-ready knowledge with Foundry IQ

Use Foundry IQ to build a knowledge base for agentic retrieval over enterprise content. Connect your documents and configure retrieval to surface relevant context for complex questions. Create an agent that brings together information across sources to deliver answers grounded in your data.

This is a self-paced, digitally-delivered lab experience that you will complete on your own schedule. Click the 'Launch' button to start the lab.

NOTE: This lab will be available to complete on November 17, 2026, starting at 12:00 PM Pacific Time.
